category_title: Students with autism who communicate via typing and require significant wait time for responses
minimal_context: Shaffer is sitting in the front row during a class period to participate in group work with his classmates.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Shaffer, it is time for group work. Please discuss the assignment with the classmates at your table.

STUDENT: (Sits as a silent young man in the front row staring straight ahead, tapping his thumbs together.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and start talking to them.

STUDENT: (Types slowly) I think it’s so difficult to initiate conversation questions if you don’t have a teacher in the introduction.

TUTOR: I am sitting right here next to you. Just tell them your thoughts.

STUDENT: (Continues staring straight ahead and tapping his thumbs together, unable to connect with the other kids) I look to an adult to really make the bridge... adults must quietly step into the background, camouflaging their help.

options.A: Identify a friendly peer and specifically ask them to partner with the student during group work and free periods.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to initiate conversation during group work and free periods.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each group work task and free period activity.
options.D: Apply increasingly serious disciplinary measures if the silence continues, such as classroom suspension, detention, and school suspension.
